slides.say: A cone-shaped container with base radius root six and height twelve is full of water. Which of the following empty containers can hold all the water?
So first we need to know how much water there is. That's the volume of the cone. Then we look for a container whose volume is the same, or bigger.
Let's start with the math way. A cone is a pointed solid. So, like in the first lesson, its volume is the base area, times the height, divided by three.
The base is a circle, so its area is pi r squared. The square of root six is six, so the base area is six pi.
Now times the height, twelve, and divided by three. Twelve divided by three is four. And six pi times four is twenty-four pi. So there's twenty-four pi of water.
How much is twenty-four pi? We don't need pi exactly. Pi is more than three point one four, and less than three point one five.
at: Pi is more than three point one four

slides.say: First the lower end, twenty-four times three point one four. We take the three first. Twenty-four times three is seventy-two.

Now twenty-four times point one four. That's fourteen hundredths, so first we calculate twenty-four times fourteen. Twenty-four times ten is two hundred forty. Twenty-four times four is ninety-six. Together, three hundred thirty-six.
Make that hundredths, and we get three point three six.
Now we add the two parts. Seventy-two plus three point three six is seventy-five point three six. So the water is more than seventy-five point three six.
at: Now we add the two parts
Seventy-two plus three point three six

slides.say: Now the upper end, twenty-four times three point one five. The three gives seventy-two again. Point one five is a tenth, plus half a tenth. A tenth of twenty-four is two point four, and half of that is one point two. Together that's three point six.
Seventy-two plus three point six is seventy-five point six. So the water is less than seventy-five point six.
So the water is between seventy-five point three six and seventy-five point six. That's more than seventy-five, and less than seventy-six.
Now the choices. If a container's volume is the same as the water, or bigger, all the water fits. If it's smaller, it's out. And for each container we ask first, is it straight or pointed?
Choice number one says, a cube with edge four. A cube is a straight solid, edge times edge times edge. Four times four times four is sixty-four.
Sixty-four is less than seventy-five, so it's less than the water. Choice number one is out.
Choice number two says, a square pyramid with base edge six and height seven. A pyramid is pointed. So it's the base area, times the height, divided by three.
The base is a square, six times six, thirty-six. Thirty-six divided by three is twelve. And twelve times seven is eighty-four.
So the pyramid holds eighty-four, and the water is less than seventy-six. All the water fits. In the exam you'd circle it and move on. Here, let's check the others too.
Choice number three says, a box measuring six by four by three. A box is straight, so we multiply its three edges. Six times four is twenty-four, and twenty-four times three is seventy-two.
at: a box measuring six by four by three

slides.say: Careful here. If you take pi as just three, the water is exactly seventy-two, and this box looks big enough. But pi is more than three point one four, so the water is more than seventy-five. This box is too small. Choice number three is out.
at: But pi is more than three point one four

slides.say: Choice number four says, a cylinder with base radius root two and height ten. The square of root two is two, so the base is two pi. Times ten, that's twenty pi.
at: a cylinder with base radius root two

slides.say: Twenty pi is less than twenty-four pi, so choice number four is out too.
at: so choice number four is out

slides.say: So again, straight or pointed? Straight, the base area times the height. Pointed, the same, divided by three. Only the pyramid holds all the water. Choice number two is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number two is our answer
